candidate_relations.reason: Acute motor axonal neuropathy is an axonal motor variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome; the generic label omits the benchmark subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Parent syndrome without the required acute motor axonal neuropathy subtype.

candidate_relations.reason: Classical GBS/AIDP is a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, whereas the benchmark diagnosis is acute motor axonal neuropathy.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Demyelinating GBS subtype conflicts with the required axonal motor subtype.

candidate_relations.reason: ALS is typically a chronic progressive disorder with upper and lower motor-neuron findings, not the acute postinfectious areflexic paralysis represented by acute motor axonal neuropathy.
AIDP and acute motor axonal neuropathy are distinct Guillain-Barré subtypes defined by demyelinating versus axonal pathology.
